Definition: to weave (i.e. lay) a trap; figuratively, (through the idea of secreting) to allay (passions; physically, abate a flood)
BiblicalUsage: Shakak is to allay or abate, to make a flood or a wrath subside. God made a wind to pass over the earth and the waters were assuaged after the flood, and the wrath of King Ahasuerus was appeased after Vashti was gone. The same word lays a trap, for wicked men lie in wait as one who sets snares to catch men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God can abate a flood and a king's wrath with the same ease, and both are His to still.
